messages:
nina: Flagging a regression after the 22:30 change window. Canary to v7.0.0 shows p95 drift on /v1/stream started ~22:33 UTC.
omar: deploybot posted: "rollout v7.0.0 canary=12% region=global started 22:28". Any auto-revert rules?
deploybot: auto-signal: p95 > threshold for 5m. Autorevert policy=warn-only in this window. Suggests staged unwind but requires human ack.
felix: I prefer manual. We have a mix of hosted and dedicated routes; a global auto-revert might be noisy.
tara-ops: Agreed. Proposal: staged unwind limited to dedicated pools first (12%->0% over 4m), hold for 15m; if metrics normalize, pin previous version for dedicated and open PR to revert canary manifests.
zoe-product: I'll prep a short customer-facing blurb in case we pin. Keep it tight: what happened, what we did, next steps.
imra-sre: (typo) sorry, ira here. We should also capture runtime flags and kernel selection traces before we revert to preserve evidence.
ira-sre: +1 on trace capture. Don't let autorevert flip before we get stack traces.
nina: who can run the traffic unshift? Omar?
omar: I can: `rictl traffic shift --service stream --from v7.0.0 --to v6.9.3 --percent 12 --scope dedicated --duration 240s`
deploybot: acknowledged; command queued.
tara-ops: running now -> response: ok shifting 12->0 over 240s on dedicated scope.
deploybot: update: canary at 9% per rollout plan.
(2m)
felix: metrics: p95 dropping as canary sheds; error rate trending down from 1.9% -> 0.8% at 6% canary. CPU on dedicated nodes also normalizing.
ira-sre: collecting kernel and kv cache counters now, grabbing traces with seqlen > 1024.
(5m)
om ar: canary for dedicated at 0% now; hosted remains paused at 12%.
nina: start pin for dedicated: `rictl pin version --service stream --version v6.9.3 --scope dedicated --note "staged unwind 22:38 UTC"` -> ok pinned.
tara-ops: opening rollback PR in infra to revert canary manifests for dedicated only: https://git.internal/infra/pull/4782 (WIP).
zoe-product: drafted customer blurb: "During tonight's maintenance window we observed elevated latency on streaming endpoints for dedicated pools. We shifted traffic back to a stable version and are investigating root cause. No data exposure." Ready to send after verification.
ira-sre: initial traces show kernel fallback to quant_path_legacy on long-context requests and higher kv cache eviction rate. Dumping trace snippets in the PM doc.
felix: given metrics back to baseline on dedicated and traces captured, recommend keeping dedicated pinned for 24h and running a focused compatibility test against v7.0.0 (long-seq stress).
(15m pass)
ira-sre: verification window complete: p95 stable and error rate ~0.3%. Draft RCA notes indicate fallback kernel selection as likely cause.
omar: merging rollback PR now to make infra state explicit.
deploybot: PR merged; infra manifests restored to v6.9.3 for dedicated canary.
nina: final decision: manual staged unwind executed, dedicated pinned to v6.9.3 for 24h pending patch. Owners: ira=RCA/traces, omar=rollback PR & pin, zoe=customer comms, tara-ops=patch scheduling. If hosted metrics show similar regression we'll re-evaluate hard revert vs targeted patch.
zoe-product: customer note sent to affected list at 23:05 UTC. Release notes updated with rollback steps and rationale.
felix: adding runbook note: prefer staged unwind + pin for mixed-hosting routes to preserve traces and avoid noisy automated flips.
ira-sre: creating postmortem skeleton in #postmortems with timeline, commands, and traces.
nina: thanks team. Closing thread for immediate operations. :thumbsup:
